arxiv-1606-04606.title: Evidence for periodicity in 43-year-long monitoring of NGC 5548
arxiv-1606-04606.creator: E. Bon, S. Zucker, H. Netzer, P. Marziani, N. Bon, P. Jovanović, A. I. Shapovalova, S. Komossa, C. M. Gaskell, L. Č. Popović, S. Britzen, V. H. Chavushyan, A. N. Burenkov, S. Sergeev, G. La Mura, J. R. Valdés & M. Stalevski
arxiv-1606-04606.description: Abstract {comment} We present an analysis of 43 years (1972 to 2015) of spectroscopic observations of the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 5548. This includes 12 years of new unpublished observations (2003 to 2015). We compiled about 1600 H β \beta spectra and analyzed the long term spectral variations of the 5100Å continuum and the H β \beta line.

arxiv-1804-06749.title: Asymptotic Expansions of Jacobi Polynomials for Large Values of 𝜷 \boldsymbol{\beta} and of Their Zeros This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Orthogonal Polynomials, Special Functions and Applications (OPSFA14). The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/OP
arxiv-1804-06749.creator: Amparo GIL †, Javier SEGURA † and Nico M. TEMME §
arxiv-1804-06749.description: Abstract Asymptotic approximations of Jacobi polynomials are given for large values of the β \beta -parameter and of their zeros. The expansions are given in terms of Laguerre polynomials and of their zeros. The levels of accuracy of the approximations are verified by numerical examples.

arxiv-2105-01680.title: On Moment Matching for Stochastic Systems
arxiv-2105-01680.creator: Giordano Scarciotti, Andrew R. Teel
arxiv-2105-01680.description: Abstract In this paper we study the problem of model reduction by moment matching for stochastic systems. We characterize the mathematical object which generalizes the notion of moment to stochastic differential equations and we find a class of models which achieve moment matching.

arxiv-2309-07910.title: TEMPO: Efficient Multi-View Pose Estimation, Tracking, and Forecasting
arxiv-2309-07910.creator: Rohan Choudhury, Kris M. Kitani, László A. Jeni, laszlojeni@cmu.edu
arxiv-2309-07910.description: Abstract Existing volumetric methods for predicting 3D human pose estimation are accurate, but computationally expensive and optimized for single time-step prediction. We present TEMPO, an efficient multi-view pose estimation model that learns a robust spatiotemporal representation, improving pose accuracy while also tracking and forecasting human pose.

arxiv-2406-14518.title: Algebraic geometry of bubbling Kähler metrics
arxiv-2406-14518.creator: Yuji Odaka
arxiv-2406-14518.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuji Odaka. We give an algebro-geometric or non-archimedean framework to study bubbling phenomena of Kähler metrics with Euclidean volume growth, after [ DS17 , Sun23 , dBS24 ] . In particular, for any degenerating family to log terminal singularity, we give an algorithm to algebraically construct a finite sequence of birational modifications of the family with milder degenerations, and partially relate with analytic bubbling constructions in [ Sun23 , dBS24 ] . We also provide equivalent approaches in terms of coordinates and valuations.

arxiv-2411-19391.title: A New LISA-Detectable Type Ia Supernova Progenitor in the Southern Sky: SMSS J1138 − - 5139 Facilities: Gemini South (Zorro), Magellan:Baade (MagE spectrograph),
arxiv-2411-19391.creator: Alekzander Kosakowski, Matti Dorsch, Warren R. Brown, Thomas Kupfer, Fatma Ben Daya, Mukremin Kilic
arxiv-2411-19391.description: Abstract We present the discovery and analysis of a nearby eclipsing ultra-compact accreting binary at coordinates 11:38:10.91 − - 51:39:49.15 (SMSS J1138 − - 5139), the first well-constrained LISA-detectable Type Ia supernova progenitor. Our time series optical spectroscopy identifies its orbital period through radial velocity monitoring at P orb , RV = 27.69 ± 0.03 ​ min P_{\rm orb,RV}=27.69\pm 0.

arxiv-2501-06133.title: Testing conditional independence under isotonicity
arxiv-2501-06133.creator: Rohan Hore, Jake A. Soloff, Rina Foygel Barber, Richard J. Samworth
arxiv-2501-06133.description: Abstract We propose a test of the conditional independence of random variables X X and Y Y given Z Z under the additional assumption that X X is stochastically nondecreasing in Z Z . The well-documented hardness of testing conditional independence means that some further restriction on the null hypothesis parameter space is required.

arxiv-2505-11397.title: Weakly-Coupled Trace Anomaly Action for Gravity
arxiv-2505-11397.creator: Gregory Gabadadze
arxiv-2505-11397.description: Abstract \mciteSetSublistLabelBeginEnd We discuss a local, diff-invariant quantum effective action for gravity that captures the trace anomaly via a counter-term. We discuss why this counter-term is most significant among infinitely many possible ones, and show how the counter-term leads to a scattering amplitude that is strongly coupled at arbitrarily low energies.

arxiv-2509-18677.title: X-ray emission of F-type stars and its analogy with G-type stars
arxiv-2509-18677.creator: Takuma Shimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi, Masanobu Kunitomo, Shinsuke Takasao, Yuki A. Tanaka, Koki Sakuta
arxiv-2509-18677.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Takuma Shimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi, Masanobu Kunitomo, Shinsuke Takasao, Yuki A. Tanaka, Koki Sakuta. We conducted a systematic spectral study for single F-type main-sequence (MS) stars without significant X-ray outbursts to investigate X-ray spectral properties such as temperature, emission measure (EM), and luminosity ( L X L_{\rm X} ). To this end, 33 single stars with relatively rich X-ray photon statistics were selected by cross-matching large astronomical catalogs of the XMM-Newton source catalog and the Tycho-2 spectral type catalog.

arxiv-2509-22315.title: PRIME: Planning and Retrieval-Integrated Memory for Enhanced Reasoning
arxiv-2509-22315.creator: Hieu Tran, Zonghai Yao, Nguyen Tran, Zhichao Yang, Feiyun Ouyang, Shuo Han, Razieh Rahimi, Hong Yu
arxiv-2509-22315.description: Abstract Inspired by the dual-process theory of human cognition from Thinking, Fast and Slow , we introduce PRIME (Planning and Retrieval-Integrated Memory for Enhanced Reasoning), a multi-agent reasoning framework that dynamically integrates System 1 (fast, intuitive thinking) and System 2 (slow, deliberate thinking).

pmc-10616615.creator: Nourou Dine Adeniran Bankole, Adyl Melhaoui, Yasser Arkha, Semmar Afaf, Khalid Bouyakhlef, Mahjouba Boutarbouch, Mohamed Jiddane, Abdeslam El Khamlichi
pmc-10616615.description: BACKGROUNDBrain metastases (BMs) are the most common expansive intracranial lesions in adults. Approximately 50% of patients diagnosed with new brain metastases have more than one brain metastasis at the time of diagnosis.OBJECTIVEWe report our experience of brain metastases treated with GKSR and evaluate the outcome.

pmc-11675305.title: The Roles of Phytohormones in Plant Defense Mechanisms Against the Brown Planthopper
pmc-11675305.creator: Huiying Wang, Wenjun Zha, An Huang, Yan Wu, Shaojie Shi, Lei Zhou, Aiqing You, Jianhui Ma
pmc-11675305.description: The brown planthopper (BPH; Nilaparvata lugens Stål) is the most significant insect pest compromising rice production globally. Phytohormones, which are small organic compounds produced by plants, play a crucial role in regulating plant growth and development. Nevertheless, extensive research has established that phytohormones are essential in modulating plant defense against BPH.

pmc-12712100.title: AAV-delivered engineered suppressor tRNA rescues visual function in mice with an inherited retinal disease
pmc-12712100.creator: Chengda Ren, Li Song, Ming Hu, Xiu Jin, Licong Liang, Fanfei Liu, Jing Su, Jiamei Fu, Yiliu Yang, Man Liu, Qiuxia Xu, Xiaoyi Wu, Min Luo, Qin Ye, Qiqi Li, Yifang An, Manjun Li, Kaiqin She, Yuquan Wei, Fang Lu, Yang Yang
pmc-12712100.description: Nonsense mutations change a sense codon into a premature termination codon (PTC) in mRNA and account for approximately 18.5% of human inherited retinal diseases (IRDs)-related mutation. Nonsense suppression therapies by small molecular drugs or suppressor tRNAs (sup-tRNAs) can introduce an amino acid at PTC, thereby promoting the production of full-length proteins.

pmc-12737192.title: Acute Decrease in Glenohumeral Internal Rotation During Repetitive Baseball Pitching Is Associated with Transient Structural Changes in Medial Longitudinal Arch of Stride Leg: Pilot Study Using Mixed Model
pmc-12737192.creator: Takeru Abekura, Noriaki Maeda, Tsubasa Tashiro, Satoshi Arima, Ryosuke Kaizuka, Madoka Koyanagi, Koshi Iwata, Haruka Yoshida, Ginji Ito, Mayu Ueda, Takashi Yamada, Tim Doyle
pmc-12737192.description: Pitching requires effective transfer of ground reaction force (GRF), and structural breakdown of the medial longitudinal arch (MLA) may influence glenohumeral internal rotation (IR) deficits. This study investigated whether changes in foot morphology of the stride leg and soft tissue characteristics are associated with loss of IR during repeated pitching.

pmc-13290500.title: Molecular Interplay of PARN and Telomerase: Tail Modifiers and Disease Implications
pmc-13290500.creator: Sujitha Felicitus, Shalon Suzanne Pinto, Sai Samanvitha Madagundapalli Ramakrishna, Dechamma Pandyanada Nanjappa, Gunimala Chakraborty, Anirban Chakraborty
pmc-13290500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Poly(A)‐specific ribonuclease (PARN) and telomerase are two indispensable tail‐modifying enzymes that are required in two critical cellular processes: the control of the rate of RNA stability and maintenance of telomere integrity, respectively. Pathogenic variations in genes that code for PARN and telomerase complex enzymes have been implicated in several rare genetic diseases, including bone marrow failure syndromes, telomere biology‐related disorders, and neoplastic ailments.

pmc-13634186.title: Deciphering transcriptome complexity via long‐read sequencing
pmc-13634186.creator: Chuwen Xu, Jia Li, Chenxi Yin, Keying Li, Tian Wang, Shiwen Gao, Yue Yu, Cheng Chang, Ye Wang, Guoqing Tong, Liang Gong, Wen Hu, Guoliang Chai, Yilai Han, Qian Qin, Suoqin Jin, Xiufen Zou, Bo Li, Tianyuan Zhang, Ana Conesa, Yunhao Wang, Dingjie Wang
pmc-13634186.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transcriptomics is moving beyond gene‐level quantification toward isoform‐resolved interrogation of alternative splicing, transcript structural variation, and repeat‐derived transcription. Yet short‐read sequencing remains intrinsically limited in accurately reconstructing full‐length transcripts and resolving complex repetitive regions, including transposable elements. Recent advances in long‐read sequencing, exemplified by Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), offer a transformative opportunity to directly observe complete RNA molecules and thereby overcome these bottlenecks.
